nh_hero_block.blurb: Hero Block is a single granite boulder in the Blair Woods cluster at Pawtuckaway State Park, and it is the first block you meet when you take the left fork on the circuit trail. Ten problems wrap around it, from a handful of easy V0 warm-ups through a middle band of V3 to V5, up to a V6 and a V7 line. The harder problems reward good friction and careful footwork. The woods around it are quiet, so you can usually have the block to yourself, and the easy sides make it a decent stop for mixed groups.

nh_apocalypse_walls.blurb: Apocalypse Walls is a small cluster of three short walls on the hillside above The Meadows at Rumney. It is mostly a sport crag, with eight bolted lines plus one trad route and one aid line, and the grades tilt hard: a couple of easy options at the bottom of the range, then a solid block of 5.11s, a few 5.12s and one 5.13. The rock is noticeably steeper than at The Meadows below, and the walls stay cool in summer. The left side tends to hold seepage, so bring a tarp for the rope. It gets far less traffic than its neighbour, which helps on busy weekends.

nh_the_asylum.blurb: The Asylum is a compact sport wall in Rumney's northwest crags, sitting just up the slope from the Prudential wall. It holds ten routes, nine of them bolted and one on trad gear. Three routes are in the 5.7 range, which makes it a useful stop for a gentler pitch, but the real draw is the cluster of six 5.11s, with a single 5.12 at the top end. Several of the middle-grade lines here are well regarded, so expect steady use on good days. It suits climbers who are comfortable on sustained, technical face climbing at the upper grades.

nh_choss_overhang.blurb: Choss Overhang is a steep, overhanging block in the woods near Willard Pond in the Monadnock region, a short walk off the trail beyond a stone bench. It is the standout block of the pond's boulders, with powerful, board-like moves between flat or incut edges. Eleven problems are recorded, running from V3 up to V11, and most of them sit in the V9 to V11 range, so this is a spot for strong boulderers rather than a warm-up venue. Several projects and link-ups are still open. Cold, dry days suit the textured rock best, and the setting is quiet with few other climbers around.

nh_alchemy_wall.blurb: Alchemy Wall is a sport crag within Russell Crags in Merriam Woods, in Woodstock, set directly above the Bird Murder cliff. Ten bolted lines cover a wide range, from a 5.6 and a 5.8 for easier days to a dense group of 5.11s, with a couple of 5.12s and one 5.13 at the top. Several of the moderate and mid-grade routes carry good ratings and are worth the hike, and the 5.10 to 5.11 range is the main attraction. It has a quieter, early-development feel compared with the larger walls nearby.
